limits: Refuses a format the recorded history cannot produce.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: An export: the construction history written in the format asked for, with nothing inferred; the Provenance panel's reading is on the history itself.
bio.jane/contract.question: Write this construct's recorded build as the document named.

description: Write a construct's recorded build out as a document: a methods section, a step spreadsheet, the full decoded record, the molecule carrying its own history as GenBank qualifiers, the whole strategy as an OpenCloning document, the runnable QUEEN script that rebuilds it, or the build as an SBOL 2 document. This is the Export tab of the History & Provenance panel (the same seven writers), refusing the same formats that source cannot produce.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

document.description: File id or name. The focused document when omitted, exactly as the panel.

format.description: which document to write. `methods` is the default because it is the panel’s first row and the only one every source can produce; the other six each need something of the record, and asking for one a source cannot carry is refused by name rather than answered with an empty file. Values: methods (Methods (Markdown)), steps_csv (Steps (CSV)), record_json (Full record (JSON)), genbank (GenBank with construction history), opencloning (OpenCloning document (JSON)), queen_script (Reconstruction script (Python)), sbol (SBOL 2 construction record).

sbol_syntax.description: which RDF syntax to write the SBOL record in. SBOL is RDF and the six concrete syntaxes encode ONE graph, so this changes how the document is written down and never what it says. `rdfxml` is the default because it is what the writer composes and what libSBOLj validates; the rest are re-serialised from that exact document. Ignored unless `format` is `sbol`, and saying so is refused rather than silently dropped. Values: rdfxml (RDF/XML), turtle (Turtle), ntriples (N-Triples), nquads (N-Quads), trig (TriG), jsonld (JSON-LD). Only applies when format is sbol.

name: export_construction_record

available.description: the formats THIS record can produce, and for each one it cannot, why: the panel’s own enabled/disabled derivation, so a pipeline can branch on it instead of failing

caution.description: what the panel warns about after this write, when it warns. Empty is the healthy case: a GenBank whose construct carries no other annotation will not read its own history back, and the file looks perfect either way

filename.description: the name the panel saves it under, so a pipeline writing several agrees with it

format.description: the format actually written: echoed because it is defaulted, not required

source.description: which of the 5 records this was written from: the workbench log, a SnapGene .dna reaction graph, a QUEEN build script, an OpenCloning strategy, or an SBOL 2/3 construction record

syntax.description: the RDF syntax the SBOL record was written in, echoed because it is defaulted. Empty for every other format, which do not have one

text.description: the document itself, byte for byte what the panel’s download writes
